newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed, backs off morning highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed, backs off morning highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed Thursday, backing off morning highs that resulted from some shortcovering, industry sources said.
"Several marketers got caught short this morning, but now we have (several) sellers in the market," said one New York based futures broker.

As of 1235 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 14 cents at $36.20 from the day's low of $36.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) and after hitting a new contract high of $37.30, while September was steady $30.15 following exchanges in a range of $29.80-30.80 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 23 cents at the day's low of $23.10 after hitting a high of $23.50, while September was down 59 cents at the day's low of $22.50 following a high of $23.50 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1125 EDT an estimated total of 228 PV and 43 COB contracts had traded.
The futures were said to be weaker on expectations of several generation units returning to service through July, and despite some immediate significant unit outages, the sources said.
In generation news, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada remained off line with no estimate as to how long it would be shut.
The unit, which tripped off Monday due to a boiler tube leak, had been expected to restart late Wednesday night, but the discovery of additional tube leaks led to the delay.

Also, in the Northwest, Washington Public Power Supply System said Thursday it has taken its 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant briefly off line to make repairs to the unit's generator. The repairs were expected to be completed by later today and the unit back on line by Friday.
WNP-2, in Richland, Wash., has been in the process of returning to operation following its refueling and maintenance which began in late March.

The 1,073 MW unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant in California reached 90 percent power as of early Thursday and was expected to reach full power by 1200 PDT, Pacific Gas & Electric, the plant's operator, said.

Overnight the unit was ramped down to 60 percent capacity for repairs to its condensate system. The unit, which was shut last week because of problems with its feedwater system, had reached 75 percent early this week.

The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be shut Friday for three weeks. The unit needs work to repair a ground, or dead spot, in its high pressure generator field.
Restarts of the 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating (SONG) Station, in San Clemente, Calif., were set for July 15 and July 17.
Separately, due to maintenance, capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was set to be trimmed by 450 MW between 0900 and 1600 on Friday, the Bonneville Power Administration said.
Cool, wet weather is expected to linger over the Pacific Northwest into the weekend, followed by warmer, drier conditions next week.
Meanwhile, seasonably hot and arid conditions are predicted for most of the Southwest through next week.
